question.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is considered the father of this nation, which split from India in 1947. This nation still disputes the Kashmir province with India.
question.clue: This nation lost the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971.

swap.leadin: Before World War I, this man had a major work, Hind Swaraj, published in South Africa.
swap.text: Name this nonviolent leader of India's independence movement who was assassinated by Nathuram Godse.
swap.clue: He encouraged his countrymen to join him on a protest known as the Salt March.

question.text: The Mughal dynasty was founded by this man, who conquered much of Northern India after the Battle of Panipat in 1526.
question.clue: Rana Sanga of Mewar ("MAY-ver") was poisoned by his own Rajputs to prevent a second conflict with this ruler, the first of which ended at the Battle of Khanwa.

swap.text: This emperor, the grandson of Akbar, was confined to Agra Fort by his son Aurangzeb when he fell ill in 1658. Name this ruler who constructed the Taj Mahal for his late wife Mumtaz Begam.
swap.clue: His son Shuja led one of the factions in the succession war that followed this man's 1658 illness.

question.text: This Indian territory was returned to the Indians in 1961. The Dutch tried numerous times to conquer this territory which was named the capital of Portuguese India in 1843.
question.clue: Much later, this state became part of a union territory along with the exclaves of Daman and Diu on the coast.

swap.text: Company rule came to an end after this rebellion. The spark for this rebellion came after a rumor spread that the British greased their Enfield rifle cartridges with pig and cow fat.
swap.clue: Beginning in Meerat, it was wiped up by Sir Hugh Rose, and Sir Colin Campbell oversaw the operation in Lucknow.

question.leadin: This nation's 1951 revolution overthrew the ruling Rana dynasty.
question.text: Name this country, which at the time was governed by King Tribhuvan. Tribhuvan opposed the Ranas, and in response Prime Minister Mohan Shumsher declared Tribhuvan's grandson king.
question.clue: This country supplies gurkha soldiers to the British Army, and this country's Sherpa people are part of its Buddhist minority.

swap.text: This competing empire named for a rebellious caste from a particular state was predominantly Hindu and arose in reaction to Mughal Emperor Aurengzeb's intolerant religious policies. After defeating the Mughals despite losing the Third Battle of Panipat this empire was eventually conquered by the British.
swap.clue: The position held by the Bhat family in this empire was that of Peshwa, and that held by Shuha and his grandfather was Chhatrapati.

question.leadin: Name these female politicians of the last twenty years.
question.text: This leader of the Pakistan's People's Party served two terms as president.
question.clue: This leader's father developed their country's nuclear weapons program with the Chagai-1 tests.

swap.text: The prince Sri Lumay was half-Malay and half-[this ethnicity]. The three great kingdoms to rule these Dravidian peoples were the Chola, Chera, and Pandyas.
swap.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

question.leadin: This group assassinated President Premadasa in 1993.
question.text: Name this terrorist group that wanted to form a separate state from the rest of the Buddhist Sinhalese population.
question.answerHtml: Tamil Tigers [or Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam; or LTTE; prompt on Tigers]
question.clue: This group, based out of Kilinochchi, suffered its final defeat at Mullaitivu.

swap.leadin: This revolt was partly caused by the introduction of rifle cartridges greased by pig and cow fat.
swap.text: Name this revolt of 1857 in which Indian soldiers rebelled against British officers. The British Raj was formed after this revolt.
swap.answerHtml: Sepoy Revolt [or Sepoy Rebellion or Sepoy Mutiny; prompt on Indian Rebellion of 1857]
swap.clue: Post offices were special targets of one side in this event, which began in the town of Meerut.

question.leadin: A monarch of this kingdom, Rajendra I, sent a military expedition to bring the water of the Ganges back to its capital.
question.text: Name this kingdom in Southern India that at its height extended its rule to the Malay peninsula. This kingdom was defeated by the Pandyas in the 13th century.
question.clue: Similar theories about the occupation of Northern India often propose that survivors of the Indus Valley Civilization fled South to establish three kingdoms in the Deccan: Chera, Pandya, and this largest Tamil empire.

swap.text: Germany later helped establish the Indian Legion, a military force led by this head of Azad Hind. This man revamped the Indian National Army.
swap.clue: One force created by this man and trained by Nazi Germany participated in Operation Bajadere.

question.text: The Ghaznavid empire's early expansion came at the expense of a confederacy of this Indian ethnic group, at the time led by the Paramaras and Pratiharas. A king of these people, Rana Sanga, challenged Babur at the Battle of Khanua, while Akbar stabilized Mughal relations with this group by agreeing to have sex with one of their princesses, whom he renamed Mariam.
question.clue: An entire ruling family of these people called the Guhilas was wiped out in 1303 after the capture of the Chittor Fort.

swap.text: Bulgarian Khans worshipped near a 100-meter tall rock carving of a horseman crushing one of these animals at Madara. Trevor Bryce claims the first coat-of-arms of Europe in Mycenae depicted one of these animals, which appeared on gates to the entrance of Hattusa.
swap.clue: Pairs of these animals that were sculpted with cloth balls under one of their paws often stood at the entrance of imperial Chinese buildings.

question.text: The Amritsar protestors were expressing opposition to these laws, which addressed Indian sedition by removing the rights of warrant, habeas corpus, and appeal from those subject to the British Raj.
question.clue: Also known as the "Black Acts," name this 1919 legislation which was passed over the unanimous opposition of the Indian members of the Supreme Legislative Council.

swap.leadin: Alluri Seetharama Raju launched the Rampa rebellion during this campaign, which expanded tactics like symbolic promotion of "self-reliant" spinning of khadi cloth from the earlier Swadeshi Movement.
swap.text: Name this post-World War I satyagraha movement promoting boycotts of British goods and denial of labor that supported British rule in India. The later Salt March re-affirmed the value of its intended non-violent approach.

question.text: A more militant attempt at independence was driven by this leader of the Indian National Army, who allied with Japan against the British. A rival of Mohandas Gandhi, he was a two time president of the Congress Party before leaving to form the Forward Bloc and later dying in a mysterious plane crash.
question.clue: He formed a separate party known as the Forward Bloc and controversy still surrounds his supposed death in a plane crash over Taiwan, since there are reasons to suspect he was in Russia at the time.

swap.leadin: One apocryphal account in this religion's history holds that the sixty-nine-year-old Baba Deep held his severed head on his body while storming a holy city in 1757.
swap.text: Name this religion whose members were massacred in the Chhota and Wadda Holocausts, which occurred in 1746 and 1762 at the hands of Lakhpat Rai and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
swap.clue: That monarch who followed this religion defeated the Afghan king Zaman Shah to capture Lahore, then declared himself a maharaja.
